answer: Registration locks a vote-escrowed stake that cannot move as a slashable bond: an identity costs real money. Detection runs on audits sampled every epoch: any agent caught failing a random proof-of-work audit is flagged. Conviction means half the bond is cut and the remainder frozen for ten epochs. No identity exists without its own bridge of locked funds. The registry maps each sonnet to exactly one bond, never two. A nectar that breaks the rules loses its bond the same epoch.
